title: AI in your creative team: who decides what
hook: Before you add AI to a creative team, write down which decisions stay with people.
caption:
Before you add AI to a creative team, write down which decisions stay with people.

Most teams are comfortable with AI doing the reading: tagging ads, counting what repeats, flagging what is slowing down.

The doubt starts when a tool changes spend or approves creative and cannot say why.

So agree the split first. AI reads and suggests, with reasons. A named person decides anything that spends or goes live.

That is how we built Galvor: it never touches the media budget.

Save the questions on the last slide for your next vendor call.

slides.headline: AI in your creative team: *who decides what?*
slides.sub: A simple split to agree before you switch anything on.

slides.headline: The fear is a tool that *acts* and cannot explain itself
slides.body:
Most teams are fine with AI doing the counting.

The doubt starts when it changes budgets or approves creative, and nobody can say why.

slides.headline: Three rules for *any AI* in the team
items: Every suggestion comes with its reasons
A named person approves anything that spends
Anyone can ask why and get a plain answer

slides.headline: Galvor *never touches* the media budget
slides.body:
Our digital co-worker, Vira, shows its thinking with each recommendation to scale, cut or shift.

Your team reads the reasons and makes the call.

slides.headline: Ask this before any AI tool *goes live*
items: What can it change without a person?
Can it show why it suggested this?
Who signs off on what goes live?

slides.headline: Let AI read. *Let people decide.*
slides.sub: Save this for your next vendor call.
